notes: FROZEN -- daemon=incapable, not recordable, so no phases are asserted. Hermes DOES sample a real quota counter per API call: agent/rate_limit_tracker.py parses the twelve x-ratelimit-* headers into four buckets exposing limit/remaining/reset and a derived usage_pct, and agent/credits_tracker.py parses x-nous-credits-* into remaining_micros/used_fraction; run_agent.py::_capture_rate_limits / _capture_credits refresh both after every streaming API call. But the reading lives only on agent._rate_limit_state / agent._credits_state in the agent process (agent_init.py:875) and is consumed only by print paths (cli.py::_show_usage:10568, gateway/slash_commands.py:4421, the CLI status bar); /usage appends nothing to the message list that gets flushed to the store. $HERMES_HOME/state.db -- the adapter's single Source (agent.ProcessOwnedStore over StorePath(), permission 'store') -- has no limit/remaining/reset/used_percent column on sessions or session_model_usage, no rate-limit table, and no message row carrying the printed output (verified: 0 matching rows on a live store). --usage-file (hermes_cli/oneshot.py:127-166) reports cumulative tokens/cost/model/session_id only, no counter. And lifecycle.Event carries no rate-limit field / KindRateLimit, so the sidecar could not hold it either. querySessionMetrics therefore never sets SessionMetrics.RateLimit, and the scenario's Windows[0].UsedPercent progression + advancing SampledAt are unobservable -- no recording could satisfy them. The CORRECT behavior (a non-decreasing UsedPercent with SampledAt advancing turn-over-turn) is documented here and is NOT weakened; it becomes assertable once hermes persists the captured window into the store (or grows an irrlicht-facing transport) AND the adapter projects it. Model is deliberately NOT pinned -- there is no recording to confirm it from.
